title: Evidence
description: A normalised, storable claim that supports or undermines a decision. Evidence is what the analyst reads and what every rationale must point at. It deliberately CANNOT hold a message body - only a claim, a pointer back to the source, and at most one short redacted quote.

source_type.description: Where this claim came from. 'identity' covers KYC / identity-assurance findings.

source_ref.description: Id of the originating object: comm_771, txn_018, adv_0032, cust_1042.

claim.description: One sentence, human readable, stating what this evidence asserts. The LLM may write this, but it must be entailed by the signals - never invented.

confidence.description: Calibrated confidence that the claim holds. Carried forward from the contributing signals.

timestamp.description: When the underlying event occurred, not when we processed it.

signal_refs.description: The signals that produced this claim. Provenance - an evidence item with no signals and no policy rule behind it is a bug.

critical.description: True when this evidence alone is enough to force the top of the ladder, e.g. a confirmed remote-access request. Critical evidence MUST be consumed before a decision can be proposed.
